title: NWSL terminates media rights agreement with Victory+ over non-payment: Sources
content:
The NWSL has terminated its media rights agreement with the streaming platform Victory+, ending a partnership that lasted less than a year, the league announced on Thursday. The split is due, in part, to unfulfilled payments, sources within the league told The Athletic.

Beginning with Sunday’s matches, every game previously scheduled to air on Victory+ will instead stream free on NWSL+, the league’s direct-to-consumer platform. The league said the move will not affect its broadcast schedule and fans will continue to have free access to the impacted matches.

The NWSL did not comment on the reason for the immediate termination of its agreement with Victory+, and the streaming platform did not immediately respond to a request for comment on this story.

The decision comes amid mounting uncertainty around Victory+, which has recently seen multiple leagues exit the platform.

Earlier this month, MLB’s Texas Rangers announced they were ending their partnership with the platform midseason, while the NHL’s Anaheim Ducks informed the platform that they also intend to terminate their agreement.

According to Sports Business Journal, which first reported the news, Victory+ has had difficulty securing additional financing since February. It also reported that Victory+ has had equal trouble funding its minimum-guarantee payments to teams across multiple leagues.

Victory+ joined the NWSL’s media portfolio ahead of the 2026 season as the league sought additional distribution to support an expanded schedule. With expansion clubs Boston Legacy and Denver Summit increasing the league to 16 teams, the NWSL’s calendar grew to 248 matches, including the Challenge Cup and playoffs. The free, ad-supported streaming service was scheduled to carry a weekly Sunday night package with a live alt-cast, including former players Ali Riley and Kelly O’Hara and a handful of streamers, along with dozens of additional regular-season matches through the 2027 season, totaling 57 NWSL matches.

One of the biggest criticisms of the NWSL’s record-breaking four-year, $240 million media rights deal has been accessibility. Fans hoping to watch every match must juggle multiple broadcasters and streaming subscriptions. Victory+ partnership aimed to ease that burden while also broadening the league’s reach.  When speaking with The Athletic a month ago, Victory+ CEO Neil Gruninger said the platform was not only driving reach for the NWSL but also accelerating fandom. According to Gruninger, a quarter of NWSL viewers on the platform have watched “six or more matches this season, and the average viewer has tuned in for four games.

The move does not affect the NWSL’s other media agreements. National broadcast windows on CBS Sports, ESPN, Prime Video and ION will continue as scheduled.
